_what_this_is: What one scored submission costs on the pinned card, broken down by stage. `eval/round.py` computes how many submissions fit an interval from this, so it is an artifact rather than a constant in the source.
_method: Stage boundaries were read from the mtimes of the artifacts each stage writes (gate-base.json, gate-cand.json, raw.json, receipt.json) for a full run of eval/score_submission.sh. That is a legitimate measurement and a poor instrument: it is why eval/gate.py now records its own `wall_seconds` and eval/bench.py records `wall_s` per record, so the next run produces this directly instead of by inference.
_cache_note: The base arm's gate is cached per base commit, so a typical submission pays the warm figure. But merging a round's winner moves `main`, which invalidates that cache -- so a round that merges pays the cold gate on its next run. The round budget uses cold + n x warm.
_it_gets_cheaper: Scoring cost is proportional to how slow the runtime is, so every contribution the benchmark pays for makes the benchmark cheaper to run. Re-measure this before raising the slot count.
